STORM PREPARATION · HOMEOWNER GUIDE

A Roof Preparation Checklist for Treasure Coast Hurricane Season

Plan roof maintenance before a storm threatens: document conditions, address known damage, check drainage and prepare contact information safely.

Near Shore Roofing LLC · Published October 14, 2026 · 2 min read

IN THIS GUIDE

Do the maintenance before the forecast becomes urgentDocument the roof you haveAsk about damaged materials and vulnerable detailsKeep drainage and the surrounding property in mindKnow who to contact afterwardSchedule a conversation about existing concerns

Do the maintenance before the forecast becomes urgent

A storm warning is a poor time to discover a long-standing roof problem. Begin with known leaks, loose or damaged roofing, and drainage issues while there is time to arrange an assessment. Roof preparation is one part of a household storm plan. It cannot eliminate wind or water damage, and it does not replace local evacuation or emergency instructions.

Document the roof you have

Keep installation records, previous repair invoices, product information, and warranty paperwork together. Photograph visible roof surfaces from the ground or another safe location. Take interior photos of existing stains so you have a clear record of their condition. Store copies somewhere accessible if you must leave home. Documentation supports a better conversation with your roofer; it does not determine insurance coverage.

Ask about damaged materials and vulnerable details

Tell the contractor about missing shingles, displaced tiles, loose metal details, damaged flashings, or leaks associated with wind-driven rain. Ask whether valleys, penetrations, and perimeter details need attention. Have qualified people assess anything that requires roof access. Avoid climbing up to inspect a roof yourself, especially when surfaces are wet or weather is approaching.

Keep drainage and the surrounding property in mind

Blocked gutters and downspouts can interrupt water flow. Arrange appropriate cleaning and discuss discharge points. Have trees and dead limbs addressed by qualified professionals before storm conditions begin. The National Weather Service includes property preparation and securing outdoor objects in its hurricane guidance. Keep roof maintenance connected to the wider plan for the home.

Know who to contact afterward

Save the roofer’s phone number, your insurer’s claims contact, and local emergency information. After a storm, wait until conditions are safe, observe from the ground, and photograph visible changes. Stay away from downed lines and unsafe structures. Never assume a roof is safe to walk on because it looks intact.

Schedule a conversation about existing concerns

Near Shore Roofing lists storm damage repairs, roof repairs, and roof and gutter cleaning. Call 772-356-3443 to discuss the condition you have noticed and available scheduling. No particular response time or level of storm resistance is promised.
